Plagiarize

PLAY-juh-ryz · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To plagiarize is to take someone else's work or ideas and present them as one's own.

The software instantly flagged the passage he had plagiarized from a website he'd forgotten to credit.

Worked Example

The student was expelled after professors discovered he had plagiarized entire paragraphs from an old thesis online.

Copying whole paragraphs and presenting them as his own is exactly plagiarizing.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

copy: To copy is simply to reproduce something, and it can be completely honest — copying a class handout, copying a quotation into notes with the source shown. To plagiarize adds the crime: presenting what you took as your own original work, with the true author hidden.

pirate: To pirate a work is to copy or distribute it without the owner's permission — bootleg films, cracked software. The wrong is taking without asking or paying. To plagiarize is a different wrong: you may even have permission, but you claim the authorship.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

credit: acknowledge the true source of work

Where it sits · how far the dishonesty goes — borrow an idea → plagiarize → forge

borrow an idea vs. plagiarize: Borrowing an idea and building on it, with credit given, is a normal part of scholarship; plagiarize means taking the actual words or work and hiding the true source.

forge vs. plagiarize: Forge means creating an entirely fake document or signature, a more extreme fabrication, while plagiarize takes something real and simply mislabels its author.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Plagiarize comes from Latin plagiarius, which originally meant 'kidnapper' or 'seducer,' from plagium, 'a kidnapping.' The word's oldest sense had nothing to do with writing at all.

Use the root in a new word: plagiarism

Use the root in a new word: plagiarism: The related noun plagiarism keeps this surprising history alive -- literally, 'kidnapping' someone else's words instead of a person.

Word Building

Word Choice

Plagiarize is most often used in academic or creative contexts -- essays, articles, music, art -- for presenting someone else's work as one's own original creation.
